subject: Mythology
title: The Kami: Gods in Everything
description: Learn The Kami: Gods in Everything in one minute.

hook.text: In Shinto, gods are not just in heaven. They live in rocks, rivers, trees, mountains, and even storms.

buildup.text: These spirits are called kami. There are said to be eight million of them, filling every corner of the world.

discovery.text: A particularly old tree, a strangely shaped rock, or a powerful waterfall might be home to a powerful kami.

twist.text: Kami are not all good. Some are dangerous, angry, or mischievous — nature itself is morally neutral.

climax.text: Shinto shrines honor kami with offerings, prayers, and festivals, keeping the spiritual world in balance.

punchline.text: In Japan, the divine is not above the world. It is the world.

quiz.question: What are kami in Shinto belief?
options: Warrior spirits that protect samurai in battle
Spirits dwelling in nature, objects, and phenomena throughout the world
Ancestral ghosts that haunt old buildings
